note: Four unrelated documents, because a corpus of one cannot test whether retrieval picks the right source. Several questions turn on words that appear in more than one document with different meanings: 'notice period' ends a tenancy in the lease and a job in the handbook; 'excess' and 'deposit' are both sums you might get back; flood appears in two. Each question names the capability it exists to test, so a failure says what broke rather than only that something did.

questions.question: am I allowed to have a guide dog in the flat?
questions.targets: dense retrieval — the lease says 'assistance dog', the question says 'guide dog'

questions.question: when do I have to keep the noise down?
questions.targets: dense retrieval — 'keep the noise down' shares no content word with 'quiet hours'

questions.question: what are the rules about keeping animals?
questions.targets: the lexical arm on a conversational question — the case that was silently dead

questions.question: PM2.5
questions.targets: the lexical arm on a rare token dense retrieval blurs

questions.question: how much is the deposit and when do I get it back?
questions.targets: a figure and a period that must both survive chunking and be quoted exactly

questions.question: how much notice do I have to give my landlord before moving out?
questions.targets: picking the right source — 'notice period' is a heading in both the lease and the handbook

questions.question: how much notice must I give if I resign after three years?
questions.targets: the same confusable from the other side, and a condition (after two years) that changes the answer

questions.question: what excess do I pay on an insurance claim?
questions.targets: 'excess' and 'deposit' are both refundable-sounding sums in different documents

questions.question: is flood damage covered?
questions.targets: flood appears in the insurance policy and nowhere useful in the lease
expectedContentMarkers: Damage caused by flood is covered

questions.question: can I claim a taxi home after a late meeting?
questions.targets: an answer that is conditional rather than a flat yes or no

questions.question: what happens if my broadband is down for a week?
questions.targets: a rate that must be quoted exactly, from the least prominent document

questions.question: can I carry unused holiday into next year?
questions.targets: a limit plus a deadline, both of which must come through together

questions.question: what is not covered if the house is empty for a long time?
questions.targets: an exclusion, which is stated as a negative and is easy to answer backwards

questions.question: how much does a parking permit cost?
how many people are allowed to live at the property?
questions.targets: refusal on something a lease plausibly answers but this one does not, so related passages retrieve and the model must still decline

questions.question: what is the excess on my broadband contract?
questions.targets: refusal where the word exists in the corpus but not in the document asked about — the failure mode that looks most like a right answer
